dailyHabits.description: Keep essential tools accessible: tape measure, level, clipboard, camera, notepad.
dailyHabits.whyMatters: Prepared FEs solve problems immediately; unprepared ones have to walk back for a tool and delay the fix.
dailyHabits.example: Problem found during a walk → immediately measure, photograph, and note it → resolved in the same visit instead of a second trip.

dailyHabits.description: Work through a problem yourself before escalating — but ask real questions along the way instead of guessing.
dailyHabits.whyMatters: FEs are problem-solvers, not problem-escalators. Constantly deferring to the Super for every decision slows the whole team down and stunts your own growth.
dailyHabits.example: Layout looks off by a fraction of an inch — re-measure from two reference points and check the drawing revision before assuming it's wrong and escalating.

dailyHabits.description: Work shoulder-to-shoulder with trades; understand their constraints instead of just inspecting from a distance.
dailyHabits.whyMatters: Workers notice — and respond to — genuine respect. An FE who's dismissive of the trades gets slower cooperation and less honest information.
dailyHabits.example: Ask a foreman why a sequence is done a certain way before flagging it as wrong; often there's a constraint you don't see from the drawings alone.

dailyHabits.description: Verify work using a different person or a different method than the original check.
dailyHabits.whyMatters: The same person using the same method tends to repeat the same mistakes. Fresh eyes — or a different tool — catch errors the original check missed.
dailyHabits.example: Laid out with a total station → verify with a tape measure. Have someone else spot-check if possible.

dailyHabits.description: Carry a pocket notebook recording daily details: weather, people on site, decisions made, measurements taken.
dailyHabits.whyMatters: Memory is unreliable, especially months later in a dispute. A contemporaneous, handwritten record is treated as strong evidence.
dailyHabits.example: Daily entry: weather conditions, crew names present, what was accomplished, and any decisions made and by whom.

dailyHabits.description: Surface issues early instead of waiting for them to compound — don't let a small problem sit hidden for days.
dailyHabits.whyMatters: Most Field Engineer failures trace back to a hidden problem that was known but not communicated until it was expensive.
dailyHabits.example: Noticed a minor spec deviation on Monday — flag it in the daily report and to the foreman that same day, not at Friday's punch walk.

weeklyGoal: Practice all 6 habits at least 5 out of 7 days
